newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Peronist government, governors agree tax sharing.
newsitem.headline: Peronist government, governors agree tax sharing.

text.p: Economy Minister Roque Fernandez and provincial governors of Argentina's ruling Peronist Party agreed Thursday on how to share revenue from his new fiscal austerity plans, governors said.

They agreed to cede to the government income from new fuel taxes included in the fiscal package to be debated by Congress next week, in exchange for a share of a 10 percent income tax hike. This was proposed by business leaders instead of the doubling of personal wealth tax favored by Peronist deputies.

"We agreed to this because we are not interested in where the money comes from, just on finally getting the resources," Santa Fe province's Governor Jorge Obeid told reporters after a Peronist conclave called by President Carlos Menem.
The government hopes to raise $600 million from whichever of these measures is implemented towards Fernandez's efforts to narrow a budget deficit he warns could otherwise hit $6.6 billion this year.
